modelName: Federation — how groups reach county scale without becoming a crowd
modelNote: A group cannot grow: Group Size → Belonging is negative in the BGTE frame, so scale destroys the very thing that makes a group able to act as one. Follett's answer in The New State (1918) is federation — you do not grow the group, you federate groups — and the whole question is whether the next level INTEGRATES or merely AGGREGATES. Aggregation is the ballot: pre-formed positions counted, majorities made, difference destroyed on the way up. Integration is the group process repeated at a higher level, producing something no member brought in. Every node carries a hover note. Drawn Aug 16 2026. REVISED Aug 16 2026: the fan-out of 7-12 is a constraint on a BODY, not a coverage plan. NDCs are not surveyed into existence — one exists wherever residents care to invest themselves in taking care of everyone in that place. So the structure has to tolerate patchy coverage, very different sizes, and groups that form, dissolve and reform.

nodes.label: You do not grow a group. You federate groups — and the only question that matters is whether the next level INTEGRATES or merely AGGREGATES.
nodes.note: Aggregation counts pre-formed positions and makes a majority. Integration runs the group process one level up and produces something no member walked in with. Both look like meetings. Only one of them is federation.

nodes.label: COUNTY · EIP LEVEL
nodes.note: Where the public goods live — the things whose scale exceeds any possible group. This level cannot be a group and should not pretend to be one. Its legitimacy comes from the return trip working all the way down, not from anyone at this level feeling close to anybody.

nodes.label: FEDERATION OF NDCs
nodes.note: The load-bearing invention. It is NOT a representative assembly and not an association of convenience — it is a group whose members happen to be groups, running the same interweaving process one level up. Your own Follett diagram: Capacity for Further Integration → Federation → Interweaving. Capacity built locally is what decides whether this body integrates or aggregates.

nodes.label: NDC · THE GROUP
nodes.note: Belonging-scale. Note the distinction that matters: the NEIGHBOURHOOD may be two thousand people, but the DELIBERATING CORE must be group-sized, because Group Size works against Belonging. The core's legitimacy comes from being open and rotating, not from having been elected to speak for everyone.

nodes.label: THE PERSON
nodes.note: Where person orders live, and where the whole structure is finally answerable. Every level above exists to hold what this level cannot hold alone.

nodes.label: Watershed · airshed · communicable disease · emergency response · codes and enforcement · the shared instruments
nodes.note: All of these fail the group test for a specific reason: their scale exceeds any group, or they are adversarial, or their failure is catastrophic and irreversible. They are the public-good cell of the sorting frame, and they are governed, never ordered.

nodes.label: Only what no single NDC can hold: commons that cross boundaries, shared standards, risk-adjusted order values, equalisation between neighbourhoods
nodes.note: Subsidiarity as a hard rule, not a sentiment. The federation may hold ONLY what a group genuinely cannot. The moment it takes something a group could have done — because it is more efficient, which it usually is — local capacity begins to atrophy, and local capacity is the thing that made the federation work in the first place.

nodes.label: Place orders · the commons of this place · the deliberative conversation itself
nodes.note: The group level of the sorting frame: rival, non-excludable, co-produced. And the conversation is not overhead — it is the production process for belonging, which is the precondition for honest verification.

nodes.label: Person orders · the dān · their own plan, and the right to say it was not met
nodes.note: The private-good cell. Singular, excludable, and verifiable by the one person who knows.

nodes.label: AGGREGATION — delegates carry mandates, the body votes, a majority forms, and difference was destroyed before anyone arrived
nodes.note: Follett's central target in The New State. If each NDC settles internally and sends one position, the interweaving has already been prevented — the federation receives pre-smoothed inputs and can only bargain over them. The result is R2 at a higher level: a crowd wearing the clothes of a democracy.

nodes.label: DETACHMENT — the upper body stops returning, becomes a professional class, and the groups become its audience
nodes.note: The oldest failure of every federated structure. The tell is easy to watch for: how long since a decision came back down and actually changed a group's view? If the return trip has quietly stopped, the federation has become a government and the groups have become constituents.

nodes.label: SCALE CREEP — the federation does what a group could do, because it is more efficient; local capacity atrophies; and the capacity was the point
nodes.note: A reinforcing decay loop, and the most seductive of the three because every individual step is defensible on efficiency grounds. Group skill is made, not found — it exists only while it is being exercised. Centralise the work and the skill goes, and with it the ability to federate well.

nodes.label: THE FEDERATION IS ITSELF A GROUP — 7 to 12 bodies, then another tier
nodes.note: Group Size works against Belonging at every level, so a federation of forty is a crowd no matter how good its members are. But read this as a rule about when a BODY must split, not as a map of how many neighbourhoods there ought to be. You do not draw the tree and then populate it — the tree grows from wherever groups actually form.

nodes.label: DELEGATES REPORT DISTRIBUTIONS, NOT POSITIONS
nodes.note: The same rule as place-order verification, for the same reason. A delegate brings the disagreement inside their NDC, not its settled view — because difference is the raw material the next level interweaves, and a delegate who arrives with a mandate has already burned it. This single rule is most of the difference between integration and aggregation.

nodes.label: ROTATION — no permanent delegates
nodes.note: Two jobs at once: it prevents a professional class forming, and it spreads the integrative skill, which is made in the doing and cannot be transferred by briefing. Rotation looks inefficient and is the mechanism by which capacity is manufactured.

nodes.label: RIGHT TO LEAVE + GRADUATED SANCTIONS
nodes.note: Straight out of your own Follett drawing, and two of Ostrom's design principles for a governed commons. A federation nobody may leave has no consent in it; sanctions that jump straight to expulsion make exit the only real option. Graduated sanctions are what let a group discipline a member without losing it.

nodes.label: THE TEST: name one decision this body made that no member walked in with. If you cannot, it is aggregating.
nodes.note: A checkable diagnostic for a thing that is otherwise all atmosphere. Integration produces outcomes traceable to nobody's opening position — that is what Follett means by the living act. If every federation decision can be traced to some member's starting demand, the body is a bargaining table and should be described as one.

nodes.label: SUCCESS TO THE SUCCESSFUL, BETWEEN NDCs — the strong get the orders, the savings and the capacity; the weak fall further behind
nodes.note: The same archetype you drew INSIDE a group, now running BETWEEN groups. An NDC with weak integrative capacity completes fewer place orders, generates fewer savings, receives a smaller share, and loses more capacity. Left alone this entrenches exactly the inequality the whole design exists to reduce, and it will look like merit the entire time.

nodes.label: EQUALISATION — capacity transfer, not only money
nodes.note: The counter-loop, and it has to move more than funds. A neighbourhood short on integrative capacity cannot buy it; capacity is made in the doing, so what transfers is time, accompaniment and rotation — people from a strong NDC sitting in a weaker one, and the reverse. Deliberately holding the federation's share unequal in favour of the weaker groups is the only way this does not compound.

nodes.label: COVERAGE IS EMERGENT, NOT PLANNED
nodes.note: An NDC exists wherever residents care to invest themselves in taking care of ALL the people in that place. It is not surveyed into existence and cannot be. So the count is unknowable in advance, coverage will be uneven, sizes will differ wildly, and groups will form, dissolve and reform. Design for that rather than for a map. Peter Block: asking 'how many' is usually a way of postponing.

nodes.label: SELF-SELECTING IN WHO ORGANISES — NEVER IN WHO IS CARED FOR
nodes.note: The load-bearing word is ALL. Whoever turns up does the organising; the care is owed to everyone in the place regardless. The moment those two collapse together you have a club good wearing the clothes of a commons — which is the exact difference between an NDC and a homeowners' association, and it is a common enough failure that it belongs in the charter.

nodes.label: A GROUP FORMS WHERE ONE COULD ALREADY HAVE FORMED
nodes.note: The failure mode that comes with emergence, and it sits one level earlier than Success to the Successful. Self-organisation correlates with time, security, tenure and prior trust — so the fragmented, displaced and frightened places are least likely to produce a group, and they are exactly the places with the worst health. Left alone an emergent design concentrates its benefits where they were least needed, and it looks the whole time like people simply choosing not to take part. The answer is not to go and organise them: an outsider convening a group produces a crowd or a clientele. What transfers is presence, invitation and accompaniment, over years, before there is anything to fund.

nodes.label: THE PERSON REGISTER IS UNIVERSAL — THE PLACE REGISTER IS EMERGENT
nodes.note: The reassuring property, and it falls straight out of having two registers. A person order needs no group to verify it — only the person. So somebody on a block that never organises still has a plan, an ME and their own signature. A coverage gap costs a neighbourhood its commons work; it never costs an individual their care.

edges.label: what I actually experience
edges.note: Not a survey response. The person's experience enters the group as material for the conversation.

edges.label: what the block decided, back to me
edges.note: The return trip at the lowest level. If it does not happen, the person has been consulted rather than included, and they will know the difference.

edges.label: the group's experience AND its disagreements — never a mandate
edges.note: This is the edge the whole design turns on. A delegate carrying an instruction converts the next level into a bargaining table before it convenes.

edges.label: the integrated result, brought back to be absorbed
edges.note: Follett's circular response. The group has to actually take the result in and let it change its view — otherwise the delegate is a politician and the loop is decorative.

edges.label: public goods, standards, and the account of what was done
inputs arrive pre-smoothed
edges.note: Breaks the UP edge. If each NDC settles internally first, the difference is gone before the federation convenes and there is nothing left to interweave.

edges.label: the return trip stops
edges.note: Breaks the DOWN edge. The body keeps meeting and keeps deciding; what stops is anything coming back that changes a group's view.

edges.label: before there is a group to fund
